questions.question: What are JSON struct tags in Go, and how do you use them?
questions.title: Json Struct Tags
questions.direct_answer: Backtick annotations on struct fields: `json:"name"` controls the JSON key, `json:"name,omitempty"` skips zero values, `json:"-"` excludes entirely. They map Go field names to wire-format keys.

sections.title: Quick Revision
sections.content: Backtick annotations on struct fields: `json:"name"` controls the JSON key, `json:"name,omitempty"` skips zero values, `json:"-"` excludes entirely. They map Go field names to wire-format keys.

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
The tag is the mapping:

```go
type User struct {
    Name     string `json:"name"`             // the JSON key is "name"
    Email    string `json:"email"`            
    Age      int    `json:"age,omitempty"`   // skip when 0
    Password string `json:"-"`                // NEVER serialized
    notes    string                          // unexported — also never
}

// Marshal(User{Name:"Al", Email:"a@x"}):
// {"name":"Al","email":"a@x"} — Age skipped (0), Password excluded, notes invisible — verified
```

The three controls the tag gives:
1. The key name: `json:"custom_name"` — the Go field and the JSON key can differ freely
2. omitempty: skip when the value is the type's zero (0, "", nil, false, empty slice/map)
3. The dash: `json:"-"` — never marshal, never unmarshal (the security boundary for Password, internal state)

The tag format is strict: the space-separated convention is `json:"key,option1,option2"`. A malformed tag silently falls back to default behavior (no error — the encoding/json package ignores what it can't parse).

The API-design use: tags ARE the wire contract. Your Go struct defines the domain; the tags define what the API looks like — and they're right there in the type declaration, greppable, diff-able, and compile-checked (unlike a separate serializer config).

sections.title: Mental Model
sections.content:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    F[Go field Name string] --> T[tag json:name]
    T --> O[omitempty: skip zero]
    T --> D[dash: never serialize]
    F --> P[Password] --> N[invisible in JSON]
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
The tag parsing, mechanically: encoding/json reads the tag via reflect.StructTag.Lookup("json") — the reflect package exposes the backtick-annotated string; the json package splits it on commas (key first, then options). A tag that fails its grammar (json:"name") — missing the closing quote — is silently skipped, not errored: the field uses the default (Go field name). No compile-time validation exists — a typo in a tag is a runtime-visible surprise.

The omitempty zero-value trap, with the fix: a struct where Age int `json:"age,omitempty"` — a legitimate age of 0 disappears from the JSON. The consumer can't distinguish 'no age' from 'age zero.' The fixes: (1) *int — nil is omitted, a pointer to 0 is included; (2) a custom MarshalJSON that checks semantic emptiness; (3) drop omitempty for fields where zero is data. The pointer is the idiom for API types where this distinction matters (counts, scores, coordinates).

The unmarshal side's tag subtlety: on decode, tags match the same way — but the case-insensitive fallback means {"Name"} fills a field tagged json:"name" (the exact match is tried first; case-insensitive is the fallback for compatibility). DisallowUnknownFields (the Decoder method) turns the default 'silently drop unknown keys' into an error — the strictness flag for contract-enforcing APIs.
